name: Redux DevTools
tagline: Action log and time-travel debugger for Redux-style state stores

license.notes: MIT monorepo (extension, instrument, monitors, remote, CLI). No CLA found. Community project under the reduxjs org; no company owner.

backing: Community (reduxjs org). Recent work is almost entirely one maintainer: markerikson authored 79 of the ~96 commits in the last 90 days, the rest mostly renovate[bot]. Originally by Dan Abramov (2015) and Mihail Diordiev (extension). GitHub Sponsors; no company funding.

notable_users: Redux Toolkit (configureStore enables it by default)
Replay.io (ReduxActions MCP tool reads the same action/state model)
adoption.summary: The de facto devtools protocol for Redux and many non-Redux stores (Zustand, NgRx, MobX bridges speak to it). ~1.5M weekly npm downloads across its packages, plus the Chrome/Firefox extension.

maintainability.release_cadence: Irregular, bursty. Browser extension 3.2.4 (2024-09-04), 3.2.5 (2024-09-16), 3.2.6 (2024-09-20), 3.2.7 (2024-09-21), 3.2.10 (2025-04-03); npm @redux-devtools/extension 4.0.0 (2026-03-17, ESM-only). A fix wave merged 2026-09-18..20 (MV3 service-worker reconnect, message chunking, import errors) is not yet tagged.
maintainability.recent_activity: ~96 commits in the last 90 days (79 by markerikson, 14 renovate[bot]); several PRs merged 2026-09-19/20; 143 open issues.
maintainability.bus_factor: low: one active human maintainer does nearly all current work
maintainability.summary: Mature and recently revived (Sept 2026 fix wave for Manifest V3), but effectively single-maintainer; features have been stable for years.

architecture.summary: A store enhancer 'lifts' the app's reducer: every app action is wrapped as PERFORM_ACTION in a lifted store whose state is {actionsById, stagedActionIds, skippedActionIds, committedState, currentStateIndex, computedStates, isLocked, isPaused}. Time travel is just more actions on the lifted store (JUMP_TO_STATE, JUMP_TO_ACTION, TOGGLE_ACTION, SET_ACTIONS_ACTIVE, REORDER_ACTION, SWEEP, COMMIT, ROLLBACK, RESET, IMPORT_STATE, LOCK_CHANGES, PAUSE_RECORDING); skipping or reordering recomputes computedStates from the first invalidated index by re-running the pure reducer. The browser extension relays the lifted state to monitors (inspector, log, chart, slider, RTK Query, trace, test tab) over postMessage; @redux-devtools/remote + redux-devtools-cli carry the same messages over a socket for React Native or remote apps.
key_points: History is itself a reducer over a serializable lifted state: devtools commands are messages, not side channels.
computedStates caches every state; maxAge (default 50) bounds the window and COMMIT folds old actions into committedState.
skip/reorder = recompute from minInvalidatedStateIndex with the pure reducer (requires reducer purity).
lock blocks non-monitor dispatches and side effects while travelling; persist keeps history across reloads (debug_session URL key).
Import/export of the whole lifted state as JSON; serialize options plus __serializedType__ revive custom types.
Test tab generates Jest/Mocha/Ava/Tape test code from a selected action and the states around it.
trace: optional stack trace per action, opened in the editor via the Trace tab.
features{} flag set can restrict a production build to e.g. export-only.

claims.text: latency (default 500 ms): actions dispatched within the interval are batched and sent at once; set 0 to send instantly, raise it (and lower maxAge) for perf issues.
maxAge (default 50): maximum actions stored in the history; oldest removed. 'It's critical for performance.'

performance.summary: No published throughput numbers. The documented knobs (500 ms batching, 50-action window) show the design budget: a human-paced inspector, not a high-rate recorder. Large states cost serialization on every relay; Sept 2026 fixes added size-based message chunking.

agent_usability.how: No first-party agent surface. Programmatically, any client of the extension (window.__REDUX_DEVTOOLS_EXTENSION__.connect: init/send/subscribe) or of the remote socket protocol (@redux-devtools/remote / redux-devtools-cli) can receive the lifted state and send DISPATCH messages carrying lifted actions (JUMP_TO_ACTION, TOGGLE_ACTION, IMPORT_STATE…). Third-party redux-mcp (3 stars, 2026-06) exposes MCP tools to read state, list observed actions, dispatch actions and reset history over a WebSocket runtime; it does not expose jump/skip. Replay.io's ReduxActions MCP tool reads actions and per-dispatch state from a recording, post hoc.
agent_usability.integration_effort: Moderate: register the store with redux-mcp (one import + registerStoresForMCP) for read/dispatch; for real time travel an agent would need a custom bridge that speaks the remote protocol and sends lifted actions. Nothing off the shelf.
agent_usability.readback: App state (JSON) and the action list are readable via the extension/remote message stream or redux-mcp. The rendered UI is not; that needs a browser tool.
agent_usability.granular_edits: Dispatch arbitrary actions (the app's own update messages). No UI patching; state edits only through the app's reducer or IMPORT_STATE of a whole lifted state.
agent_usability.history: Model supports jump, skip (toggle), reorder, sweep, commit, rollback, import/export, lock, pause. These are reachable by protocol messages, but no maintained agent tool calls them; redux-mcp offers only 'reset history'. No fork: there is one linear staged action list.
agent_usability.summary: The best-documented human time-travel model in frontend, with history ops already expressed as serializable messages; agent access exists only as thin third-party read/dispatch bridges.

score_notes.ui_as_data: App state and action log are JSON; the UI itself is React code outside the tool's model.
score_notes.agent_drivable: Remote socket protocol + third-party redux-mcp (read/dispatch/reset) — real but thin and unofficial.
score_notes.readback: Structured app state/action history readable; no rendered view.
score_notes.time_travel: Full human time travel; the ops are messages an agent could send, but no agent tool exposes seek/skip/fork today.
score_notes.live_data_rate: Default 500 ms batching and 50-action window; built for human pace.
score_notes.teaching: Watching actions flow is a classic way to teach Redux, but no tour/narration features.
score_notes.openness: MIT, community org, no company or CLA.

steelman: Redux DevTools proved, at ecosystem scale, that time travel is cheap when state changes only through serializable messages and a pure reducer: the whole debugger is just another reducer whose state is {actions, skipped ids, committed state, cursor, cached states}, so jump, skip, reorder, commit, import/export and persist all fall out of a few dozen lines rather than bespoke recorder machinery. It is the lingua franca other stores (Zustand, NgRx, MobX bridges) adopt rather than reinvent, it carries over a socket for remote and React Native apps, it can generate regression tests from a recorded action, and its 'features' flags let a production build ship export-only bug reports. A fan would say thc-scene's time travel should simply be 'Redux DevTools' lifted reducer, for a terminal UI, exposed to agents' — and that the hard design questions (bounded history, committing old actions, locking side effects while travelling, reviving custom types on import) were answered here a decade ago.
weaknesses: History window is small by default (maxAge 50) and states are cached whole, so long sessions need tuning (Arguments.md).

Time travel re-renders but cannot undo side effects; components re-dispatching on rewind is a known pitfall (zalmoxisus/redux-devtools-extension#685; 'time travel sends wrong state' reduxjs/redux-devtools#712).
Requires serializable state and pure reducers; non-serializable values need custom serialize/replacer config.
No first-party agent/MCP surface; the only MCP bridge (n1snt/redux-mcp, 3 stars) reads/dispatches and resets but cannot jump or skip.
Bus factor of one: ~80% of the last 90 days of commits are a single maintainer; the browser extension's last tagged release is 3.2.10 (2025-04-03).
Linear history only: no named branches/forks; reorder/skip mutate the one timeline.

relation_to_scene.overlap: Same Elm/Redux premise as thc-scene: serializable State, explicit messages, pure update. Its lifted-state history is exactly the record thc-scene plans (message log + cursor + cached states) and its import/export is the planned export/import.
relation_to_scene.scene_reinvents: The history data model and its ops (jump, skip/toggle, commit with a bounded window, import/export, lock while travelling, pause recording). If scene builds a message log with seek, it is re-deriving instrument.ts; it should copy the shape deliberately rather than rediscover it.
borrow: Model history as a lifted reducer: history ops are messages (JUMP_TO_ACTION, TOGGLE_ACTION, COMMIT, IMPORT_STATE…) applied by a pure function, so they replay and test like everything else.
stagedActionIds + skippedActionIds + minInvalidatedStateIndex: skip/reorder by recomputing from the first invalidated index.
maxAge + COMMIT: bounded window with old messages folded into a committed base state.
lock: suppress effects (data-source commands, exec) while the cursor is in the past.
features flags per surface (e.g. export-only for untrusted agents).
Test generation from a selected message range (scene: emit a replay test from a history slice).
relation_to_scene.gap_left: No agent-callable history API (seek/diff/fork/screen_at), no rendered-frame readback at a past point, no fork/branch, no terminal or pixel output, and no teaching/narration layer.
relation_to_scene.verdict_why: It is the reference design for message-log time travel, but it is a browser-extension debugger for JS stores, not something a Rust terminal UI can use.
